elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Operative text now reads: "The Agreement may be renewed only by mutual written agreement of the parties." This is reinforced by retained IV.II (extension "by mutual written of the parties") and IV.III ("Any additional extension ... will be by mutual agreement in writing"). No unilateral Licensor extension option survives.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the edit there is no automatic renewal mechanic anywhere in Article IV — renewal occurs only on mutual written agreement, so no renewal term length is imposed on Customer.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: renewal is not automatic; the Licensee cannot be bound to a further term absent its own written agreement, so no opt-out window is required.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no automatic renewal exists, so no reminder mechanic is needed to protect Licensee from an unnoticed rollover.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Article IV contains no renewal price-uplift mechanic, and any renewal (including its pricing) now requires Licensee's written agreement, so no unilateral increase is possible.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: renewal is by mutual written agreement only, so there is no automatic rollover requiring a non-renewal notice.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no renewal price-increase mechanic exists; renewal pricing would be part of the mutually agreed renewal.

reasons: The single operation replaces only the offending sentence ("may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor") with a mutual-written-agreement renewal, which is the shortest cure for a one-sided multi-year extension right; nothing outside the RENEWAL checklist was touched.

All remaining Article IV language — the 36-month Initial Period, the Licensor's breach-termination right, its retained payment rights, and the mutual-extension mechanics in IV.II and IV.III — survives verbatim, so timing, remedies and commercial mechanics are unaffected and no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created.
The edit removes the internal inconsistency between a unilateral seven-year Licensor option and the retained mutual-extension sentences in IV.II/IV.III, rather than creating one.

Because renewal is no longer automatic, every conditional preferred and fallback element is satisfied vacuously; the redline therefore lands at the preferred position, and the underlying clause was correctly classified as a deviation (a unilateral multi-year extension is walk-away territory and fails the fallback for want of any non-renewal notice window).
